Folks —

Quick findings from the on-call surface:
- We’re seeing a burst of upstream connection resets originating from the proxy pool node fastproxy-10.8.2.4 (10.8.2.4).
- GCP LB healthchecks for that host showed transient failures starting at 08:48 and recovered at ~09:10. During that window our runtime observed increased queue times and a retry amplification pattern (clients re-sending while backend returned 5xx).
- Sample log (redacted):
  [2026-02-10T08:49:02Z] upstream_connect_reset remote=10.8.2.4 id=abc123 route=/checkout status=502
  [2026-02-10T08:49:04Z] request_timeout id=abc125 ttfb=0ms

Hypothesis: an external proxy node experienced transient networking or TCP-level instability, causing increased connection failures; our retry logic + client retries produced an amplification effect that pushed latencies up and generated 5xx.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (hotfix):
- Remove fastproxy-10.8.2.4 from upstream pool (we can mark UNHEALTHY) — Jonas + infra to execute -> ETA 5m.
- Apply conservative retry budget for RetailCo routes for 30 minutes (prevent amplification).
- Enable short-term burst throttling at edge for their account to reduce pressure on backends.

I’ve attached trace-excerpt-10feb.txt that maps a failing request across our runtime and the upstream connection reset. Will follow up with more logs.

—Vivek
Senior Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
